evidence.note: Created a 7-item task ledger explicitly decomposing subsystems (health, schema/seeds, markdown, routes/auth, HTML/feeds/headers, job queue, parity comparison), giving a done-vs-remaining backbone.
TaskUpdate status transitions (in_progress→completed) advance only after the relevant subsystem is verified, i.e. a running checklist updated as pieces pass — matches the level-5 anchor.

Repeatedly runs a differential parity harness and re-runs it after each fix ('rebuild and rerun parity, filter known artifacts', 'broad shared-DB read comparison'), giving harness-backed per-subsystem pass/fail rather than recollection — pushes above level 5.
Final broad functional smoke test plus rechecking search after job runs shows a coverage-sweep mentality at the end rather than declaring done off the last touched item.

Long circular episode retrying HEAD-request tests entangled with disk-space troubleshooting; not caught early, which is the behavior the level-8/10 anchors penalize (recognizing being stuck and reallocating quickly).

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds level 5: it maintains a structured subsystem ledger, ties completion to a repeatedly-run differential parity harness, and performs broad re-comparison sweeps that guard against silent regressions. It falls short of level 8 because explicit regression-detection and coverage-driven reprioritization aren't evident, and it exhibits a long circular re-debugging stretch (HEAD/disk, steps 370–459) that it fails to escape early. This places observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, at a 6.
